errors.text_span: Each chart is divided into multiple colored segments, each labeled with a topic category and a numerical count representing the number of items or documents assigned to that cluster. In the “AttentionInfluence” chart, the largest segment is “Education” (25), followed by “Health & Medicine” (22), “Science” (15), “Teaching & resources” (15), “History & Society” (23), and others...
errors.evidence: The description fails to identify the two-level hierarchical (sunburst) structure of the charts. It treats the inner and outer rings of categories as a single, flat list of segments, mixing parent categories (e.g., 'History & Society' with a value of 23) and child categories (e.g., 'Teaching & resources' with a value of 15) in the same list without explaining their relationship.

The description omits several categories present in the charts. For the 'AttentionInfluence' chart, it omits: 'Fin & Law (3)', 'Tech & Engineer (12)', 'Medical (6)', 'Nutrition (5)', 'Materials (2)', and 'Science & technology education (10)'. For the 'FineWeb-Edu Classifier' chart, it omits 'Materials (1)'.

The description uses the phrase "followed by," which implies a sequential order (typically descending by value), but the list of categories does not follow this order. For instance, it lists a category with a value of 15 before one with a value of 23, making the enumeration confusing and disorganized.
